extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editors of the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for submitting, reviewing, and editing research software submissions to the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS). Covers eligibility, review items (license, documentation, functionality, tests), required paper sections, formatting, COI and AI policies, and editor/reviewer expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section heading covering the criteria and procedural requirements that must be satisfied to submit a paper to JOSS (eligibility, required materials, etc.). See linked subsections (e.g., 'Must meet (all required)').

rubrics_metrics.name: What we mean by research software
rubrics_metrics.description: What we mean by research software
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of software that is appropriate for JOSS (i.e., research software packages). Used to determine whether a submission qualifies as research software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and significance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A review criterion: assess whether the software and accompanying paper have appropriate scope and sufficient significance to merit publication in JOSS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-review screening criteria (Must meet (all required))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-review screening criteria — Must meet (all required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial gate used during pre-review to determine whether a submission satisfies required minimum conditions before full review. The site also distinguishes 'Strong positive signal (not a gate, but counts in your favour)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong positive signal (not a gate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong positive signal (not a gate, but counts in your favour)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items that are not mandatory but provide strong evidence in favour of acceptance; they help reviewers/editors but are not exclusionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI Usage Policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and required disclosures about use of AI in creating submissions. Includes separate subsections for 'Author AI usage' and 'Reviewer AI usage'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software license
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review item: the repository must include an appropriate software license (open-source license consistent with JOSS policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Development history and open-source practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level review item covering how the project has been developed and whether it follows open-source practices; broken down into specific subitems (development timeline, open development, collaborative effort, good practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Development timeline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review subitem: evidence of the project's development history (e.g., commits, releases) to demonstrate maturity and maintenance status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open development
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review subitem: whether development occurs in the open (public repository, public issue tracker, public contributions) and supports transparency and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative effort
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review subitem: evidence that the project supports or is the result of collaboration (multiple contributors, community involvement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good practices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review subitem: adherence to recommended practices for open-source projects (e.g., contribution guidelines, tests, CI, clear repository structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-level review item encompassing several required/desirable documentation elements (statement of need, installation instructions, example usage, API documentation, community guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: A statement of need
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documentation element describing why the software is needed and what problem it addresses. Also appears as a required section in the software paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation instructions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation must include clear installation instructions so users can install and run the software (platforms, dependencies, steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example usage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should include examples demonstrating how to use the software for typical tasks and workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: API documentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation should describe the software's API (functions, classes, inputs/outputs) sufficient for users/developers to understand and reuse the code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation of contribution and community norms (e.g., CONTRIBUTING.md, code of conduct) to support collaborative development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functionality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review item: the software should perform the tasks described and the reviewer should verify that key functionality works as claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review item: the repository should provide tests that demonstrate and validate the software's functionality (test suite, CI integration preferred).

rubrics_metrics.name: Software paper content (required sections)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JOSS paper must include specific required sections; the documentation lists required items under 'Software paper content' and provides guidance for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the field (required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required paper section summarizing the relevant existing work and how the software fits into or advances the state of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software design (required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required paper section describing the design, architecture, and implementation choices of the software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research impact statement (required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required paper section articulating the research impact or potential impact of the software.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI usage disclosure (required)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required paper element disclosing any use of AI in the creation of the software or paper content, per the AI Usage Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review checklist (general checks)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A structured checklist reviewers can use during review; includes categories such as general checks, development history, functionality, documentation, and software paper checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest policy (authors & reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict of Interest policy for authors / JOSS Conflict of Interest Policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies and guidance for disclosing and managing conflicts of interest for both authors and reviewers. Linked under both author and reviewer guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected professional behavior for participants in the review and editorial process; reviewers and contributors should follow the JOSS Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: JOSS paper format (What should my paper contain?)
rubrics_metrics.description: JOSS Paper Format — What should my paper contain?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting and metadata requirements for the paper (article metadata, names, name parts, particles, literal names, date, affiliations, internal references), plus content/formatting details: tables and figures, equations, Markdown/inline markup, links, grid tables, figures and images, citations, mathematical formulæ, footnotes, blocks, headings, deeper nesting, lists. Also guidance for checking that the paper compiles (GitHub Action, Docker, locally).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions using proprietary languages/development environments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy guidance about whether/when submissions that rely on proprietary languages or environments are acceptable; see linked policy page for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where can the repository be hosted?
rubrics_metrics.description: Where can the repository be hosted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on acceptable hosting locations for the code repository (e.g., GitHub and other hosting services) and any hosting-related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using AI to generate code
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific guidance under the AI usage sections about the acceptability and required disclosures when AI tools are used to generate code in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Expectations (for reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for reviewers on expected time commitment for completing a JOSS review (helps set reviewer availability and workload expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: No submission fees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy/procedural note indicating that JOSS charges no submission fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations on JOSS editors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial guidance describing the responsibilities and expected behavior of editors (managing editorial process, pre-review, review, post-review tasks, responding to editorial assignments, maintaining continued attention to assigned submissions).
